claims.claim: Chabon says Le Guin conjured an entire planet into vivid existence with nothing but lines on paper.
claims.source: Michael Chabon, The Paris Review Daily, 20 November 2019
claims.quote: conjured an entire planet into vivid existence

claims.claim: Jason P. Vest says Le Guin weaves each place's contradictions, tensions, mores and rites into detailed portraits.
claims.source: Jason P. Vest, "The Re-Possessed", The Common Reader (Washington University), 30 May 2021
claims.quote: each place’s contradictions, tensions, mores, and rites into satisfyingly detailed
claims.page: early section on the Hainish novels

claims.claim: Vest says Le Guin's invented worlds convince readers they are real places rife with complex histories, cultures and characters.
claims.source: Jason P. Vest, The Common Reader, 30 May 2021
claims.quote: real places rife with complex histories, cultures, and characters
claims.page: early section on the Hainish novels

claims.claim: Vest identifies the most famous sentence of The Left Hand of Darkness as the four-word line The king was pregnant.
claims.source: Jason P. Vest, The Common Reader, 30 May 2021, quoting Le Guin
claims.page: section on The Left Hand of Darkness

claims.claim: Alison Smith calls Le Guin's prose in Very Far Away From Anywhere Else spare and clarifying.
claims.source: Alison Smith, "Her Left Hand, The Darkness", Granta, 3 January 2019
claims.quote: too taboo for her spare, clarifying prose

claims.claim: Smith describes Le Guin's genius as an amalgam of vivid prose, straight talk and revolutionary engagement.
claims.quote: vivid prose, straight talk and revolutionary engagement

claims.claim: Sherryl Vint says Le Guin is sensitive to the notion that ideologies and values are embedded in the language and metaphors we use.
claims.source: Sherryl Vint, interviewed by Cal Flyn, Five Books, 7 May 2021
claims.quote: our ideologies and values are embedded in the language and metaphors
claims.page: interview, on The Word for World is Forest

claims.claim: A commenter on the Reactor Le Guin reread picks out a five-word Le Guin sentence and calls it lovely.
claims.source: Reader comment on "Introducing the Ursula K. Le Guin Reread", Reactor comment thread

claims.claim: Terry Morris faults the Ghibli Earthsea film for giving no sense of islands in a lonely ocean.
claims.source: Terry Morris, "Earthsea and Tales from Earthsea", Steam Engine Time No. 11 (fanzine), February 2009
claims.quote: no sense of islands in a lonely ocean
claims.page: article on the Ghibli adaptation, p. 31
